name: Eleasah
overview: Eleasah was a male descendant of the tribe of Judah, identified specifically as the son of Helez according to 1 Chronicles 2:39. Beyond this genealogical note, the biblical record provides no additional details about his life or deeds. His mention serves to preserve the lineage within the tribe of Judah.
namesAndTitles: The name Eleasah means "G-d [El] has fashioned," reflecting a recognition of divine craftsmanship in his identity. This proper name is not indicated to have been given directly by God but carries a meaningful theological implication rooted in the Hebrew language.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Eleasah was the son of Helez, as noted in 1 Chronicles 2:39. Additionally, Helez is identified as the son of Sismai in 1 Chronicles 2:40, situating Eleasah within a clear paternal lineage. No further family relationships are documented beyond these connections.
scriptureSignificance: Eleasah's significance lies in his role within the genealogical records of Judah, which are vital for understanding the heritage and tribal identities important in God's redemptive plan through Israel. Though not prominent in narrative events, his inclusion in the genealogies underscores the faithfulness of Scripture in preserving the lineage from which the Messiah would eventually come. His mention helps affirm the continuity of God's promises to the tribe of Judah.
